text: For #928, refining D-0480 on how P-0881 is carried out. One size larger, a conformance check that TLC ends with its general status, 255, fails as evidence TLC can't read when one of its messages carries TLC's own code for an evaluation error raised inside a standard operator, such as <= given a boolean, Len given a non-sequence or Head given an empty sequence. The codes are the sixteen the pinned jar's standard modules raise when they evaluate: 2145, 2155, 2157, 2158, 2169, 2176 to 2184, 2266 and 2283. tlc.Result keeps the codes of a failed run's messages, in order, as Codes; a failed result's JSON carries them and every other result's JSON is as it was. A recorded value can't write a message frame, since TLC prints a string quoted with its line breaks escaped, so it can't take a code away. Words still make nothing operational, and only TLC's general status with one of these codes fails: a disk that fills, a stall, memory, a kill and TLC's other general errors still claim nothing.
